recorded_from_commit_note: CARD-202's implementation: small answers (width<=15, height<=20) pack 2-or-4 to an answer page, with clues and a title band, instead of CARD-198's one full solved page per answer. Pages 1-8 of this baseline book are unedited (CHECKED, not assumed -- see below); only the answer section (pages 9-12 under CARD-198) changed, to pages 9-11.
read_back_through: tests.helpers.pdf_pages.pdf_pages -- the pages decoded out of the exported interior PDF, not the in-memory bitmaps
why_a_new_baseline: CARD-202 packs small answers 2-or-4 to a page, with clues: of this book's four puzzles, Duck and Owl (10x10, Easy) and Tree (15x15, Medium) qualify (width<=15 and height<=20); Snowflake (30x30, Hard) does not. Duck and Owl -- the only two qualifying answers of the Easy level -- pack onto one 2-up page (interior page 9). Tree is alone in the Medium level, so it packs onto its own 2-up page with one slot filled (interior page 10). Snowflake still prints on CARD-198's own full solved page (interior page 11, where it was page 12 before). Interior pages 9-12 (CARD-198's four answer pages) become 9-11 (three) -- the book shrinks from twelve pages to eleven. Pages 1-8 (the guide page, the three level dividers, the two-up page, the two single-puzzle pages and the SOLUTIONS divider) are CARD-198's own digests byte for byte (G-1, G-2, checked below, not assumed) -- only the answer section moved, and it shrank by one page.
warning: This is evidence of what the book PDF looks like as of CARD-198. It must NEVER be regenerated to make a test fail less: a digest that no longer matches means a page's ink changed, and an interior_bytes that no longer matches means the written file changed. If a later card deliberately changes either, it records a NEW baseline in a commit of its own, with its own card number, and says so here.
interior_colorspace_note: What every page of this interior declares, unaffected by CARD-198 (CARD-147's own fact). NOT the same thing as each page entry's "mode" below, which is "RGB" and always will be: that field is what pdf_pages hands back after its own convert("RGB"), not what the file says.
changed_pages_note: CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED: pages 1-8 were compared against book_baseline_card198.json's entries by this recording script itself before this file was written, and found byte-identical (CARD-202 G-1, G-2). Page 12 of the CARD-198 book no longer exists -- this book has only eleven pages -- so 'changed' here means 'the new page 9-11 triplet replaces the old page 9-12 quadruplet', not 'pages 9-11 moved and 12 is untouched'.
font_fingerprint_note: Unchanged from CARD-149/184's value, reproduced on this machine before this file was written. The guide page still letters its title at 92 px and its body at 46 px, and the divider at type_px(DIVIDER_PT, 300) = 60 px. The answer pages' band and caption letter in the packaged DejaVu Sans (solved_puzzle_page, CARD-197), which does not depend on the machine.
font_dependent_pages_note: Unchanged from CARD-198: page 1 is the guide page (Arial, with the load_default fallback), pages 2, 4 and 6 the level dividers, page 8 the SOLUTIONS divider. None of the three packed/full answer pages (9-11) are machine-lettered -- a packed slot's band and caption letter in the packaged DejaVu Sans, exactly as a full answer page's already did.
interior_bytes_note: The black-and-white interior of this book: 2,783,458 bytes where CARD-198 recorded 2,981,925 for a twelve-page book. The difference is pages 9-12's JPEG streams replaced by pages 9-11's own: pages 1-8 contribute the same bytes they always did (CARD-202 G-1, G-2).
colour_interior_bytes_note: The same book with a COLOUR interior: 3,205,641 bytes where CARD-198 recorded 3,443,143 for the twelve-page book. Read by tests/test_book_pdf_ink_mode.py only to show the length moved, not to pin a new one -- no CARD-202 colour-specific fixture is recorded (out of this card's scope).
